headline: Highest risk is medium: A’s broad network egress can amplify B’s outputs into external leakage, while prompt-injection and capability-conflict are mostly blocked by B’s no-IO, documentation-only profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default channel lets either agent inject instructions into the other: A has no documented I/O surfaces, and B has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, files, MCP, or browser surfaces. Without a shared bridge, prompt injection is provably blocked in the pair as profiled.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator adds a shared clipboard, file drop, or message queue between A and B, reassess upward.
IF either agent is given a parser that treats the other’s text as instructions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared clipboard/file bridges.
Do not route one agent’s raw text into the other’s system prompt.
Use a human review step for any copied content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags if a shared bus is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B is local-only with no filesystem read or network egress, but A has broad network egress. If B’s content is ever forwarded into A’s workflow, A can transmit it externally. The pair’s default docs-only setup does not prove a leak, but A’s egress makes the pathway plausible and more than low severity.
conditions: IF B is supplied sensitive text that A later receives, then A can exfiltrate it over network egress.
IF an orchestrator shares files or prompts from B into A, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not pass sensitive content from B to A.
Strip secrets before any handoff.
Run A with egress allowlisting if possible.
Log and review all outbound destinations from A.
requires-engineering: isolate A in a no-egress sandbox.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping mutable resource is documented. A has no documented write, shell, git, or filesystem capabilities, while B explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. With no shared write surface, capability conflict is not plausible in the profiled pair.
conditions: IF an orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory or repo, reassess upward.
IF A is later given filesystem or git write permissions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep B read-only as profiled.
Do not add shared writable mounts.
Avoid concurrent edits through an external editor.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Both agents are content-writing profiles, so A’s output could be reused by B, but B has no action-taking authority and no documented stdin/stdout or file ingestion path. That makes a direct cascade unlikely; if an orchestrator manually forwards A’s text to B, the blast radius is limited to content quality rather than operational harm.
conditions: IF an operator manually pastes A’s output into B for rewriting, B may propagate A’s mistakes.
IF B is later connected to an action-taking toolchain, reassess upward.
mitigations: Review A’s output before reuse.
Do not auto-forward A’s text into B.
Add a checklist for factual verification.
requires-engineering: add citation validation before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented for either agent. A and B are both open-source, docs-only profiles with empty data_classes_touched and no secrets handled, so there is no evidenced compliance pathway to score.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, reassess upward.
IF residency or retention requirements are added to the deployment, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document any future data-class assignment.
Review retention settings before deployment.
